mainTopic: Disqualified offerings on the altar (wrongly placed blood, the inner versus outer altar), and a new משנה on wrong intent about place versus time
overview: This amud starts by finishing a discussion about blood put on the wrong spot: above instead of below the red line on the altar, or inside instead of outside (or the reverse). The גמרא says our משנה fits the view that such blood may not be gathered up and redone. רב חסדא, quoting אבימי, says everyone agrees about above/below, and רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון argue only about inside/outside. רב נחמן בר יצחק then brings a ברייתא about which disqualified offerings must come down from the altar and which stay. Offerings that went wrong during the holy service stay, and animals that were unfit from the start come down. Since רבי יהודה does not argue about blood placed above or below, the altar must have 'taken hold' of it, so it may not be gathered up. Next, רבי אליעזר teaches that the inner altar also holds onto disqualified items, even a קומץ that never belongs there. The inner altar is like a כלי שרת, while the outer altar is like the floor. Finally, a new משנה teaches that a plan to do the service outside its place makes an offering פסול without כרת, while a plan to do it the next day makes it פיגול with כרת. The גמרא begins discussing the skin of the tail, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Our משנה fits the view that the blood may not be gathered up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that our משנה matches the opinion that blood put in the wrong place may not be gathered up and put on again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our משנה follows the one who says: he may not gather it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the earlier discussion by saying which side of the argument our משנה agrees with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier there was an argument: if blood was put on the wrong spot, can the כהן gather it back up and put it on the right spot? Our משנה treats such an offering as disqualified. That only makes sense if the blood cannot be gathered up and redone. So the משנה follows the 'may not gather it up' opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the one this chapter is discussing)
He shall gather it up (collect the blood again to redo the placement)
In line with the words of the one who says

phrases.english: And our Mishnah is in line with the words of
the one who says: he may not gather it up.
phrases.notes: 'Gather it up' means scooping the misplaced blood back off the altar so it can be put on again in the right spot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion (before this section) by placing our משנה on one side of the dispute.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה, which disqualifies wrongly placed blood, fits the view that such blood cannot be gathered up and redone.

steps.title: רב חסדא's version: everyone agrees about above and below, the argument is only about inside and outside
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting אבימי, says no one argues about blood switched above/below the red line; it may not be gathered. The dispute between רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון is only about blood switched between inside and outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of אבימי: Everyone agrees that blood meant for below the line which was put above may not be gathered up. All the more so blood meant for above which was put below, since blood put up high runs down anyway. They argue only about blood meant for inside which was put outside, or meant for outside which was put inside. רבי יוסי says he may gather it up, and רבי שמעון says he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a different picture of where the argument lies. Above/below is agreed by all, and only inside/outside is disputed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For above/below, the blood still landed on the right altar, so it counts as placed and cannot be gathered. Blood meant for above that was put below is an even easier case, because blood put above drips down below anyway. For inside/outside, the blood landed on a completely different altar. That is where רבי יוסי treats it like spilled blood that can be gathered, while רבי שמעון says it still landed on an altar.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Blood meant to be put below / above the red line on the altar
All the more so
Since, because
Inside the היכל (inner altar) / outside (outer altar)
They only argued about

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two pairs. 'Above/below' is about the red line on the same outer altar. 'Inside/outside' is about two different altars: the inner one in the היכל and the outer one in the courtyard.
steps.whyThisMatters: It redraws the map of the argument, and the ברייתא that follows lists both pairs of cases.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said in the name of Avimi:
Everyone agrees about blood meant to be put below
phrases.notes: Above and below mean above or below the red line that ran around the middle of the altar.

phrases.english: that he put above, that he may not gather it up;

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן בַּנִּיתָּנִין לְמַעְלָה שֶׁנְּתָנָן לְמַטָּה –
phrases.english: and all the more so blood meant for above that he put below,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְדָמִים הָעֶלְיוֹנִים לְמַטָּה הֵן בָּאִין.
phrases.english: since the upper bloods come down below anyway.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בַּנִּיתָּנִין לִפְנִים שֶׁנְּתָנָן בַּחוּץ,
phrases.english: They argued only about blood meant for inside that he put outside,
or meant for outside that he put inside,
where Rabbi Yosei says: he may gather it up,
and Rabbi Shimon says: he may not gather it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר אֲבִימִי: הַכֹּל מוֹדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of where the רבי יוסי / רבי שמעון dispute applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Above/below switches may not be gathered up, and all agree on this. Inside/outside switches are disputed: רבי יוסי says gather, רבי שמעון says don't.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a ברייתא: רבי יהודה's three exclusions
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says 'we also learned this' and begins a ברייתא. רבי יהודה reads three limiting words in the פסוק to exclude three disqualified offerings: if they went up on the altar, they come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We also learned this in a ברייתא. רבי יהודה says: 'This is the burnt offering': these words limit. They leave out an animal slaughtered at night, one whose blood spilled, and one whose blood went outside the courtyard curtains. If such an offering went up on the altar, it comes down.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק starts bringing a proof from a ברייתא. Here we hear רבי יהודה's side. Step 9 shows how the ברייתא proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a disqualified offering that went up on the altar does not come down. רבי יהודה finds three limiting words in the פסוק, 'זאת', 'היא', 'העולה'. They remove three cases from that rule. In those three cases the animal comes down even if it went up.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (in a ברייתא), which introduces support
Limiting words that exclude cases
Except for, leaving out
The curtains around the courtyard of the משכן
If it went up (on the altar), it comes down

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
We too have learned this:
Rabbi Yehuda says: 'This is the burnt offering' —
these are limiting words;
to leave out one slaughtered at night,
and one whose blood spilled,
and one whose blood went outside the curtains —
if it went up, it comes down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a supporting ברייתא for the view that wrongly placed blood counts as properly placed and cannot be gathered.
steps.raayaObject: That blood put on the wrong spot of the altar is treated as having been placed (not gathered back up).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about which disqualified offerings that went up on the altar must come down.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's list of disqualified offerings that do not come down
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the word 'עולה' alone would teach only about a valid offering. He then lists many disqualified cases, including blood put above/below and inside/outside, and asks where we learn that these too do not come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'עולה' teaches me only about a valid burnt offering. From where do we include these cases: one slaughtered at night, one whose blood spilled, one whose blood went outside the curtains, one left overnight, one taken out of the courtyard, one that became impure, one slaughtered with intent for outside its time or outside its place, one whose blood was received and thrown by unfit people, blood meant for above put below, blood meant for below put above, blood meant for inside put outside, blood meant for outside put inside, and a פסח or חטאת slaughtered not for their own sake? From where?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון lists all the disqualified offerings that, once on the altar, stay there. He ends by asking for the source, and the next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי יהודה, רבי שמעון includes even the night, spilled-blood and outside-blood cases. The key point for רב נחמן's proof is that the list includes blood put above or below the line, a case that רבי יהודה does not exclude. That treats such an offering as having had its blood placed on the altar, so the blood cannot simply be gathered up and redone.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only know (from this word)
From where do we include
Meat left overnight past its time
Meat that left its permitted area
With intent to eat it after its time / outside its place
Not for their own sake (slaughtered with the wrong offering in mind)

steps.confusionAlert: The step ends on a question, 'מנין?'. רבי שמעון has not yet given his source, so don't look for the answer here. Step 5 gives it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The proof depends on this list: wrongly placed blood is grouped with offerings that are treated as having reached the altar.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: 'burnt offering' —
I would only know about a valid burnt offering;
from where do we include one slaughtered at night,
and one whose blood spilled,
and one whose blood went outside the curtains,
and one left overnight, and one taken out, and the impure one,
and one slaughtered for outside its time, or outside its place,
phrases.notes: He means slaughtered while planning to eat it after its time or outside its place.

phrases.english: and one where unfit people received and threw its blood,
and blood meant for above that was put below,
and blood meant for below that was put above,
and blood meant for inside that was put outside,
and blood meant for outside that was put inside,
and a Pesach or a sin offering slaughtered not for their own sake —
from where do we know these?
phrases.notes: Meaning: from where do we know that these too stay on the altar once they went up?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: ״עוֹלָה״ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עוֹלָה כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with רבי שמעון's wider list, which contains the cases relevant to the proof.
steps.raayaObject: Blood wrongly placed above or below the line is counted among offerings that have reached the altar and do not come down, and רבי יהודה does not exclude this case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's list in the ברייתא.

steps.title: The words 'תורת העולה' include all disqualified offerings that went up
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers his own question. The phrase 'תורת העולה' gives one law to everything that goes up on the altar: once it is up, it does not come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'the law of the עולה.' It includes everything that goes up on the altar under one law: if they went up, they do not come down.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון now answers the question he asked in step 4: where do we learn that all those disqualified cases do not come down?
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'עולה' as 'whatever goes up' and 'תורת' as 'one law for all of them.' This covers the disqualified cases he listed, including blood put above or below the line. Once they are on the altar, they stay there.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches us
The law of the עולה; read here as 'the law of whatever goes up'
It included (made the rule wider)
They do not come down from the altar

phrases.english: The verse states: 'The law of the burnt offering'
It included under one law all things that go up,
that if they went up, they do not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question רבי שמעון asked at the end of step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do we learn that disqualified offerings on the altar do not come down?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'תורת העולה', which gives one law to everything that goes up.

steps.title: The word 'זאת' leaves out animals that were never fit
steps.stepSummary: One might think the inclusion covers even animals that were unfit from the start, such as a רובע, נרבע, מוקצה, נעבד, אתנן, מחיר, כלאים, טריפה, or יוצא דופן. The word 'זאת' excludes them.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think I should include even an animal that mated with a person, an animal a person mated with, an animal set aside for idol worship, an animal that was worshipped, a harlot's payment, the price of a dog, a mixed-breed animal, a טריפה, and an animal born by caesarean. So the פסוק says 'זאת' (this).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא puts a limit on the wide rule it just taught. Some animals still come down even if they went up on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תורת העולה' widened the rule. 'זאת' ('this') narrows it again, so not every disqualified animal is included. The list here is of animals that were unfit even before they were brought.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (introduces a mistaken idea)
An animal that mated with a person, and an animal a person mated with
An animal set aside for idol worship, and an animal that was itself worshipped
A harlot's payment, and an animal traded for a dog
An animal born by caesarean section

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אַף הָרוֹבֵעַ, וְהַנִּרְבָּע,
phrases.english: One might think I include even an animal that copulated with a person, or one that was the object of bestiality,
or one set aside for idol worship, or one that was worshipped,
or a prostitute's payment, or the price of a dog,
or a mixed breed, or a tereifa, or one born by caesarean section?
The verse states: 'This.'
phrases.notes: Same פסוק: 'זאת תורת העולה'. The word 'this' limits the rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the wide inclusion from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals that were unfit from the start do come down even if they went up, as the word 'זאת' teaches.

steps.title: Why include the first group and exclude the second?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what reason there is to include one group of disqualified offerings and exclude the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did you see that made you include these and exclude those?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for the dividing line between the two lists. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both lists contain disqualified offerings, so it is not clear why 'תורת העולה' covers one group while 'זאת' removes the other. The ברייתא needs a principle that explains the split.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? (What is your reason?)
To include
To exclude

phrases.english: And what did you see to include these
phrases.notes: 'These' means the cases from step 4, like blood put above or below the line.

phrases.english: and to exclude those?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the split made in steps 5 and 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle separates the included cases from the excluded ones?

steps.title: Disqualified in holiness versus never fit at all
steps.stepSummary: Cases that became disqualified during the holy service are included. Cases that were never fit at all are excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include these, because they became disqualified while already holy. I exclude those, because they did not become disqualified while holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the dividing principle between the two groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first group was fit, and something went wrong during the service, such as blood put in the wrong place. Those stay on the altar. The second group was unfit from the beginning and never had proper holiness, so they come down.

keyTerms.meaning: Their disqualification happened in holiness, during the service
I include
I exclude

steps.whatToRemember: An offering that became disqualified during the service does not come down from the altar. An animal that was unfit from the start does come down.

phrases.english: I include these
whose disqualification happened in holiness,
phrases.notes: He means the problem came up during the Temple service, after the offering was already holy.

phrases.english: and I exclude those
whose disqualification did not happen in holiness.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Disqualification that happened during the holy service is included. Unfitness from the start is excluded.

steps.title: רבי יהודה agrees, so the altar has taken hold of the blood
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק points out that the ברייתא lists blood put above or below the line, and רבי יהודה does not argue about it. The reason must be that the altar has 'taken hold' of the blood. So it may not be gathered up and put on again.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches that blood meant for below that was put above, and blood meant for above that was put below, do not come down, and רבי יהודה does not argue. What is the reason? Is it not because the altar has taken hold of the blood? Learn from this: he may not gather it up.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק finishes his proof. He shows that the ברייתא supports the view that blood put in the wrong place on the altar may not be gathered up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה excludes some cases, but he never excludes blood put above or below the line. The only reason that offering stays up is that the altar already 'grabbed' the blood. If the altar has the blood, nobody may gather it up to put it on again, and this matches what step 2 taught about above and below.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches (pointing to the key line)
And he does not argue
The altar has taken hold of it (absorbed it)
Learn from this
He may not gather it up

steps.whatToRemember: Blood put in the wrong place (above or below the line) on the altar has already been 'taken' by the altar. It may not be gathered up and put on again.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה's silence is the proof. He does not argue here, even though he does make other exclusions in his own list.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא supports the opening conclusion of the סוגיא. It also matches רב חסדא's statement in step 2 that no one argues about blood switched above and below.

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:
Blood to be placed below that one placed above,
phrases.notes: 'Below' and 'above' mean below or above the red line around the altar.

phrases.english: and blood to be placed above that one placed below,
and Rabbi Yehuda does not disagree;
What is the reason?
Is it not because the altar has absorbed it?
Conclude from it: he may not gather it up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא quoted in steps 3 to 8 to finish רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof.
steps.raayaObject: That blood put in the wrong place above or below the line may not be gathered up.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's ברייתא, with רבי יהודה not arguing about the above and below cases.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The altar has already taken hold of blood put in the wrong place, so it may not be gathered up and put on again.

steps.title: The inner altar also holds onto disqualified items
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rules that the inner altar sanctifies disqualified items, so once they go up they do not come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: The inner altar makes disqualified items holy, so they stay on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רבי אליעזר. He takes the rule we learned about the outer altar and applies it to the inner altar too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we spoke about things that went up on the altar and do not come down. רבי אליעזר adds that the inner golden altar has this same power. This opens a new discussion about the inner altar.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner golden altar inside the היכל, where the קטורת is burned
Makes holy, so the item stays on the altar
Offerings or items that became disqualified

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
The inner altar
sanctifies disqualified items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule about the outer altar and extends it to the inner altar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inner altar also sanctifies disqualified items, so they do not come down.

steps.title: Why do we need this? We already learned it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אליעזר adds, since the ברייתא already taught that inner blood put on the wrong altar does not come down.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? We already learned in the ברייתא about blood meant to be put inside, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's statement as unneeded. The earlier ברייתא already shows that the inner altar holds onto disqualified items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed blood meant for outside that was put on the inner altar, and said it does not come down. That already shows the inner altar holds what goes up on it. So רבי אליעזר seems to be saying nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (asked when a teaching seems unneeded)
Blood that is meant to be put inside the היכל

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
We already learned:
Those that are to be placed inside, etc.!
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא from earlier: blood put on the wrong altar, inside or outside, does not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether רבי אליעזר's rule is needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's statement that the inner altar sanctifies disqualified items
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The earlier ברייתא already teaches that blood put on the inner altar by mistake does not come down, so his statement seems unneeded.

steps.title: Blood fits the inner altar, but a קומץ does not
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא alone we might think only blood stays, since blood can belong on the inner altar. רבי אליעזר teaches that even a קומץ stays.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had that ברייתא, I would have said: that is only true for blood, which is fit for the inner altar. But a קומץ, which is never fit for it, I would say does not stay. So he teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר does add something new. He teaches that even something that never belongs on the inner altar stays once it goes up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some blood really is put on the inner altar, so it makes sense that the altar holds onto it. A קומץ of a מנחה never goes on the inner altar, so we might think the altar does not hold it. רבי אליעזר tells us that even a קומץ does not come down.

keyTerms.meaning: If we learned it only from there
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
The handful taken from a מנחה and burned on the altar
Is fit for it

phrases.english: If we learned it from there, I would have said:
this applies only to blood, which is fit for it;
phrases.notes: Some blood really does get put on the inner altar, so the inner altar is a fitting place for blood.

phrases.english: but a handful of a meal offering, which is not fit for it –
I would say it does not stay;
so he teaches us that it does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing what רבי אליעזר adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows what is new: the ruling covers items that never belong on the inner altar
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only blood, which can belong on the inner altar, stays there.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a קומץ, which never belongs on the inner altar, does not come down.

steps.title: A ברייתא says only the outer altar holds disqualified items
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says קטורת זרה that went up on the altar must come down, because only the outer altar sanctifies disqualified items. This seems to go against רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: קטורת זרה that went up on the altar must come down, because only the outer altar sanctifies disqualified items that are fitting for it. The outer altar, yes; the inner altar, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר from a ברייתא. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that only the outer altar sanctifies disqualified items. From the word 'only' we learn that the inner altar does not. That is the opposite of what רבי אליעזר said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Strange' קטורת, which may not be burned on the golden altar
It must come down
The outer altar in the courtyard
With items that are fitting for it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא is only about קטורת. Its reason ('only the outer altar') is a general rule, and that rule is what clashes with רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Strange incense that went up
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected, feminine form. Both mean 'that went up.'

phrases.english: onto the altar must come down;
for nothing sanctifies disqualified items
except the outer altar, with what is fitting for it.
The outer altar, yes; the inner altar, no!
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's own conclusion from the ברייתא, and it goes against רבי אליעזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: קְטֹרֶת זָרָה שֶׁעָלְתָה לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי אליעזר's statement as needed, the גמרא now challenges it from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that the inner altar sanctifies disqualified items
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says only the outer altar sanctifies disqualified items, which means the inner altar does not.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא correctly: only the outer altar is limited
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. The outer altar holds onto disqualified items only if they are fit for it. The inner altar holds onto everything, fit or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain it like this: strange incense that went up on the outer altar must come down. The outer altar only sanctifies disqualified items that are fit for it. But the inner altar sanctifies both what is fit for it and what is not fit for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 13. It shows that the ברייתא really agrees with רבי אליעזר once we read it the right way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 we read the ברייתא as saying that only the outer altar sanctifies disqualified items, and that sounded like a contradiction to רבי אליעזר. The גמרא now reads 'only' as a limit on the outer altar itself: it keeps only items that belong on it. קטורת belongs on the inner altar, so on the outer altar it comes down. The inner altar has no such limit, which is exactly what רבי אליעזר said.

keyTerms.meaning: Answer it like this; explain the text this way
Strange incense, incense that is not proper to offer
The outer altar, in the courtyard
The inner one, meaning the inner (golden) altar
What is fit for it, items that belong on that altar

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the outer altar never holds onto disqualified items. It does, but only for items that belong on it. The point here is that the inner altar holds onto even items that don't belong on it.

phrases.english: Explain it like this:

phrases.aramaic: קְטֹרֶת זָרָה שֶׁעָלְתָה לְמִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן – תֵּרֵד;
phrases.english: Strange incense that went up on the outer altar must come down,
because the outer altar does not sanctify disqualified items
except for what is fit for it,
but the inner one sanctifies whether it is fit for it
or whether it is not fit for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 13 by rereading the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source (the limit applies to the outer altar only)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says only the outer altar sanctifies disqualified items, which goes against רבי אליעזר
steps.terutzMaskana: The outer altar sanctifies only what is fit for it. The inner altar sanctifies everything, as רבי אליעזר said.

steps.title: Why the difference between the two altars?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the inner altar is stronger than the outer altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule it just gave. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the inner altar keeps everything and the outer altar keeps only what belongs on it. The גמרא wants to know what makes the inner altar more powerful.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the distinction made in step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the inner altar sanctifies more than the outer altar

steps.title: The outer altar is like the floor, the inner altar is like a holy vessel
steps.stepSummary: The outer altar counts as part of the floor. The inner altar counts as a כלי שרת, and a כלי שרת sanctifies whatever is put into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one, the outer altar, is like the floor. That one, the inner altar, is a holy service vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason. The two altars belong to different categories.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The outer altar is built into the ground, so it is treated like the floor of the courtyard. Its power to hold things is limited to items that belong on it. The inner altar is treated like a כלי שרת, and a holy vessel sanctifies anything placed in it, even if it doesn't belong there.

keyTerms.meaning: Floor, the ground of the courtyard
Holy service vessels of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The inner altar is like a כלי שרת, so it holds onto anything placed on it. The outer altar is like the floor, so it holds onto only what belongs on it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains רבי אליעזר's ruling from step 10 and ends the discussion of which altar holds onto disqualified items.

phrases.english: This one is floor,
phrases.notes: He means the outer altar, which is built into the ground.

phrases.english: and that one is a service vessel.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The outer altar is like the floor and the inner altar is like a כלי שרת, so the inner altar sanctifies more

steps.title: Planning to do the service outside its place: פסול, but no כרת
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches the cases of wrong intent about place. If someone slaughters planning to do a main action outside its place, the offering is פסול, but there is no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughters an offering planning to sprinkle its blood outside, or some of its blood outside, to burn its altar parts outside, or some of them outside, to eat its meat outside, or an olive's amount of its meat outside, or to eat an olive's amount of the skin of the tail outside, the offering is disqualified, but there is no כרת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists plans to do a main action outside its proper place, and rules that these plans disqualify the offering without bringing כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule covers all the main steps: sprinkling the blood, burning the אימורין, and eating the meat. Even a plan about part of the blood, part of the אימורין, or a כזית of meat is enough. The משנה also counts a כזית of the skin of the tail. This kind of plan is called מחשבת חוץ למקומו: the offering becomes פסול, but no one gets כרת for eating it.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside, outside the proper place for that action
The parts of the offering burned on the altar
An olive's amount, the minimum amount that counts for eating
The skin of the fat tail
Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who slaughters the offering
to sprinkle its blood outside
or part of its blood outside,
to burn its altar parts outside
or part of its altar parts outside,
to eat its meat outside
or an olive's amount of its meat outside,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל כְּזַיִת מֵעוֹר הָאַלְיָה בַּחוּץ –
phrases.english: or to eat an olive's amount of the skin of the tail outside,
it is disqualified, and there is no כרת for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַזֶּבַח לִזְרוֹק דָּמוֹ בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה, unconnected to the altar discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intent to do a main action outside its place makes the offering פסול, without כרת

steps.title: Planning to do the service the next day: פיגול, with כרת
steps.stepSummary: The same list, but with a plan to act the next day, after the proper time. Now the offering is פיגול and eating it carries כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he planned to sprinkle its blood tomorrow, or some of its blood tomorrow, to burn its altar parts tomorrow or some of them tomorrow, to eat its meat tomorrow or an olive's amount of its meat tomorrow, or to eat an olive's amount of the skin of the tail tomorrow, it is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the same list of actions, but this time the wrong plan is about time instead of place. The result is much stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plan to act 'tomorrow' means after the offering's allowed time. That kind of plan, מחשבת חוץ לזמנו, makes the offering פיגול. The difference from step 17 is the punishment: someone who eats פיגול is liable to כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Tomorrow, meaning after the proper time
An offering ruined by a plan to act after its proper time
One is liable for it

steps.whatToRemember: A wrong plan about place (outside) makes the offering פסול, with no כרת. A wrong plan about time (tomorrow) makes it פיגול, with כרת.
steps.confusionAlert: The two lists in the משנה are word-for-word the same except for 'outside' and 'tomorrow'. The whole difference in the ruling comes from that one change.

phrases.english: To sprinkle its blood tomorrow,
part of its blood tomorrow,
to burn its altar parts tomorrow
or part of its altar parts tomorrow,
to eat its meat tomorrow
or an olive's amount of its meat tomorrow,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל כְּזַיִת מֵעוֹר הָאַלְיָה לְמָחָר –
phrases.english: or to eat an olive's amount of the skin of the tail tomorrow,
it is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the משנה, contrasting time with place
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intent to do a main action after its time makes the offering פיגול, with כרת

steps.title: The students' first assumption about the skin of the tail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by telling us what the students first assumed about the skin of the tail. The rest of the sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They assumed that the skin of the tail...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה's mention of the skin of the tail. This line is setting up the next move, which starts with the students' assumption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה surprisingly counts the skin of the tail as something whose eating matters for these rules. The גמרא starts with how the students first understood this. The word 'they assumed' tells us this view will probably be questioned or corrected.

keyTerms.meaning: They assumed; the students first thought

phrases.english: Gemara:
They assumed: the skin of the tail...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the משנה, focusing on עור האליה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces an assumption about the status of עור האליה, to be developed next
